name: Hemostasis drill
description: An open trench through skin and fat crosses two perforating vessels. One is arterial. Control both: grasp and buzz, or decide to tie.

education.goal: Achieve hemostasis of both bleeders in the trench with less than 5 ml of blood loss and no char plug left behind.

failurePoints.consequence: Char plug over an open lumen; rebleeds later as a hematoma.
failurePoints.teaching: Grasp first, then buzz the forceps so the walls are apposed when the collagen denatures.

failurePoints.consequence: Current spreads through the pool: wide shallow burn, nothing sealed.
failurePoints.teaching: Suction and pressure first; identify the vessel; then treat it.

failurePoints.consequence: Delayed bleeding from a vessel thought controlled.
failurePoints.teaching: A plug is not a seal. Re-grasp and buzz, or tie.

decisionPoints.prompt: This bleeder is about 1 mm. Buzz the forceps, or tie it?

options.label: Buzz forceps
options.outcome: Seals reliably up to ~1.5–2 mm when coapted; marginal above that.

options.label: Tie
options.outcome: Always secure; slower. Preferred above 2 mm.

ambiguity.description: Which of the two vessels is arterial is not visible until it bleeds.
A few seeded small perforators may also be in the trench wall.
